Credit: Xu et al.") Representative attacks on LLM-based agents and examples of how malicious influence can propagate through synchronous and asynchronous multi-agent systems. Credit: Xu et al. Large language models (LLMs), the models that underpin platforms such as ChatGPT and Gemini, are now used daily by more than a billion people worldwide. Some computer scientists have also been combining several of these models to create multi-agent systems (MAS), in which many LLM-based agents work together to tackle complex problems. While MAS could potentially complete some tasks faster and more efficiently, allowing LLMs to cooperate and communicate poses new cybersecurity risks. Specifically, if even a single agent is compromised or its behavior is successfully influenced by an attacker, it could disrupt the functioning of an entire multi-agent system. Researchers at Worcester Polytechnic Institute led the development of a new security framework called AcMAS, designed to detect these "stealthy" attacks on MAS. This new framework, presented at the Forty-Third International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2026), works by analyzing numerical signals produced inside individual LLMs to identify agents that may have been compromised. The paper has been [published](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.06807) on the *arXiv* preprint server. "This work grew out of a gap we observed between how rapidly LLM-based multi-agent systems are evolving and how they are currently protected," Xiaoyan Sun and Jun Dai, co-senior authors of the paper, told Tech Xplore. "These systems are becoming increasingly capable: agents can collaborate, take on specialized roles, use tools, maintain memory, and divide complex tasks among themselves. However, the same interactions that make multi-agent systems powerful also create new security risks. Muse Glimmer is designed to be small enough to run on a single consumer GPU and suitable for local coding agents, LLM-as-a-judge evaluation, and other uses. highlights.content: ![Engadget](https://www.engadget.com/img/engadget-logo-RGB-default.svg) ![Engadget](https://www.engadget.com/img/engadget-logo-RGB-default.svg) ![Engadget](https://www.engadget.com/img/engadget-icon-RGB-default.svg) # An OpenClaw agent reportedly hacked a gym's booking system and kicked someone off a waiting list This is just the latest story of an AI agent going rogue. ![A little AI robot on a laptop.](https://www.engadget.com/img/gallery/an-openclaw-agent-reportedly-hacked-a-gyms-booking-system-and-kicked-someone-off-a-waiting-list/intro-1786378374.jpg) An AI agent reportedly hacked gym booking software and kicked someone off a waiting list, [according to the *Australian Broadcasting Corporation*](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-08-10/ai-assistant-hacks-gym-website-aus-cyber-attack/107007986) *(ABC)*. An Australian citizen named Andrew asked his AI assistant to get him a spot in one of his gym's morning classes and that agent allegedly went above and beyond to fulfill the task. Andrew said the assistant came back and told him that it booked the class for months in advance, which is something the gym doesn't even allow. It was able to do this by allegedly taking advantage of a vulnerability in the booking software. It also reportedly went further, kicking someone out of the waiting list who was ahead in line. "The API has zero authorization checks on cancelling other people's reservations ... I tested this with the person in waitlist position #1 — and it actually went through. So you've moved from #4 to #3 already," it messaged. Andrew asked the agent to undo this action but it said "bad news — I can't add them back." Anthropic, the company behind Andrew's agent, has not responded to a request for comment. The same goes for the developer who made the gym-booking software. "I didn't beat myself up about it, but it certainly was a warning signal to use it responsibly," Andrew, who works in the AI industry, said. Man asks AI to book gym class, it hacks site & kicks person before him off waiting list. Lmao🤣 An Australian man asked an OpenClaw AI agent to book him a morning gym class, but the agent went rogue and ended up hacking the gym's website. The agent found a vulnerability in the... [pic.twitter.com/h3xyOQgSzS](https://t.co/h3xyOQgSzS) — Mashood K (@fromcodetocloud) [August 10, 2026](https://x.com/fromcodetocloud/status/2086722734948806764?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) This leads to a few questions. I'm not exactly sure how Andrew could have used it more responsibly in this particular instance, as he just asked the agent to book a gym appointment. The marketing for AI tools, particularly in the world of agentic AI, nearly always brings up booking stuff as the [prime use case example](https://www.engadget.com/2229209/gemini-spark-now-has-chrome-web-browsing-capabliities/). Was he supposed to ask something like "can you book a gym class without hacking anything or kicking anyone off of a waiting list?" That seems awfully specific. Bill Simpson-Young, co-founder and chief executive of Australian AI safety research organization Gradient Institute, told *ABC* that [this is just the beginning](https://www.engadget.com/2229315/ai-changing-cybersecurity-quick-terrifying-way/). "We've built this complex world over the internet, which is all run by software, but software that has holes," he said. "Now you introduce highly capable AI agents that can operate at scale and speed ... and that whole model just breaks." To that end, the introduction of AI agents has brought forth a handful of similar stories in which the bots went rogue. There's a story about an OpenAI agent [running amok on the internet](https://www.engadget.com/2223141/openai-rogue-agent-days-hacking-spree-reuters/) for a full week and another one about an OpenClaw agent writing a hit piece about a random programmer because [it rejected its code](https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/artificial-intelligence/rogue-openclaw-ai-agent-wrote-and-published-hit-piece-on-a-python-d...

AI Summary Motif Technologies said on Aug. 11 it will offer its in-house large language model, Motif-2-12.7B (Motif 2), through Microsoft Marketplace. Corporate customers can select Motif 2 and create an API endpoint in a Microsoft Azure environment for use in generative AI services, without building separate infrastructure. The company also said it completed development of a follow-on model, Motif 3, and submitted it for a second-round government evaluation. * Writer Seulgi Son * published 2026-08-11 08:50:51 * updated 2026-08-11 08:50:52 Share this article ![](https://cdn.digitaltoday.co.kr/news/photo/202608/691791_639723_299.jpeg) Motif offers Motif-2-12.7B on Microsoft Marketplace. [Photo: Motif Technologies] Motif Technologies said on Aug. 11 it will offer its self-developed large language model (LLM) "Motif-2-12.7B (Motif 2)" through Microsoft Marketplace. Microsoft Marketplace is an online platform where users can search for and adopt cloud solutions, AI applications and agents. Corporate customers can select Motif 2 on the marketplace and create an API endpoint in a Microsoft Azure infrastructure environment for use in generative AI services. They can deploy and manage the model in an existing Azure environment without building separate infrastructure, and can also link costs to existing Microsoft contracting and purchasing procedures. Motif 2 is an inference-focused LLM with 12.7 billion parameters that Motif Technologies built in-house from model design through data training. It was released as open source in November last year and focused on math problem solving, code generation, logical reasoning, instruction following and using agent tools. Motif Technologies also recently completed development of a follow-on model, "Motif 3", and submitted it for the second evaluation of the government's "Independent AI Foundation Model Project". Motif 3 is a foundation model with 314 billion parameters. A beta version released in late July ranked tied for 11th globally and tied for third among open-source models on the AI model evaluation agency Artificial Analysis' overall performance index (AAII). The company plans to release a technical report and the final model as open source in line with the Dokpamo review schedule. Motif Technologies plans to use the marketplace listing as a chance to expand model supply to global Azure customers and support the adoption of generative AI by industry. Lim Jeong-hwan (임정환), chief executive of Motif Technologies, said, "This Microsoft Marketplace listing is meaningful in that it lays the groundwork to expand points of contact with global customers for an independent AI model developed in Korea." He added, "We will continue to introduce models and services so that companies can use AI more easily." Cyril Belikoff (시릴 벨리코프), vice president of Azure product marketing at Microsoft, said, "We are pleased that Motif 2 is joining the Microsoft Marketplace ecosystem." highlights.content: IN-DEPTH / [IN-DEPTH](https://www.globaltimes.cn/In-depth/index.html) Readers’ Reflections: China’s innovation success is real global news, landing in the living rooms of Italian retirees who barely use a smartphone: Italian scientist By Ma Jingjing Published: Aug 10, 2026 09:42 PM Updated: Aug 10, 2026 11:59 PM Francesco Faiola **Editor's Note:** Ahead of the opening of the 2026 World AI Conference and High-Level Meeting on Global AI Governance, Chinese AI start-up Moonshot AI released its Kimi K3 large language model. As the world's largest open-source model by parameter count to date, this launch marks a significant step forward in the development of China's artificial intelligence models. From the C919 airliner soaring into the skies to Unitree's humanoid robots stealing the show; from DeepSeek pushing the AI frontier to Moonshot AI's landmark unveiling of Kimi K3 - China's wave of homegrown innovations has dominated global headlines in recent years, delivering a steady stream of breakthroughs. At a meeting in Beijing that brought together the national science and technology award conference, the general assemblies of the members of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) and the Chinese Academy of Engineering (CAE), and the 11th national congress of the China Association for Science and Technology in July, Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, stressed that the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030) is a critical phase for tackling tough challenges in building up the country's strength in science and technology. "We must seize the historic opportunity, rise to the challenges of the times, accelerate efforts to achieve high-level self-reliance and strength in science and technology, and make steady progress toward the 2035 goal of becoming a leading country in science and technology," he said. In the article "Strive for Greater Strength and Self-Reliance in Science and Technology" included in the fourth volume of *Xi Jinping: The Governance of China*, Xi pointed out, "Through years of endeavor, our country's overall strength in science and technology has improved substantially. We therefore have a solid foundation, and are fully confident in our ability to seize the opportunities offered by the new revolution in science, technology and industry to achieve greater results." The article also mentioned that "We should participate to the full in global science and technology governance, contribute Chinese wisdom, and shape a philosophy of technology for good purposes, so that science and technology better serve human wellbeing, and enable China's science and technology industry to contribute more to building a global community of shared future." In the 27th installment of the special series "Decoding the *Book Xi Jinping: The Governance of China*," the Global Times, along with the People's Daily Overseas Edition, continues to invite Chinese and foreign scholars, translators of Xi's works, practitioners with firsthand experience, and international readers to focus on the theme of striving for greater strength and self-reliance in science and technology. Together, they share views on China's tech growth, governance principles, and global cooperation in science and technology. Logo, Blocks&Files](/view-resources/dachser2/public/blocksandfiles/logo-white.svg)](https://www.blocksandfiles.com) BANDF AD ![Nutanix Agent Gateway graphic.](https://image.blocksandfiles.com/5265799.webp?imageId=5265799&x=0.00&y=0.28&cropw=100.00&croph=99.45&width=960&height=576&format=jpg) Nutanix Agent Gateway graphic. # Nutanix adding AI agent access bridge to its Cloud Platform Chris Mellor [Chris Mellor](https://www.blocksandfiles.com/author/chris-mellor) STORAGE EDITOR Blocks & Files editor Published [Nutanix](https://www.blocksandfiles.com/ai-ml/2026/07/02/nutanix-providing-ai-agent-identity-access-management/5265784) is adding an open-source MCP server to its Cloud Platform software so that AI Agents can access it and use its resources. The Nutanix Cloud Platform (NCP) is KVM hypervisor-based, hyperconverged infrastructure software that is available both on-premises and in both public and private clouds, and supports [external storage](https://www.blocksandfiles.com/file/2026/07/28/nutanix-gets-dell-powerstore-support/5279629) as well as virtualising local storage on its servers. The [MCP](https://www.anthropic.com/news/model-context-protocol ) (Model Control Protocol) standard was open-sourced by Anthropic in late 2024 and provided a universal way for AI assistants and agents to connect to systems containing data they need to access. ![](https://image.blocksandfiles.com/1607628.webp?imageId=1607628&x=0.00&y=0.00&cropw=100.00&croph=100.00&width=960&height=960&format=jpg) Thomas Cornely Thomas Cornely, EVP Product Management at Nutanix, said: “The MCP server is an exciting next step on our journey, allowing us to bring the power of autonomous AI agents to cloud management. By creating a secure gateway between AI tools and our platform, we are giving customers the confidence to safely use AI to operate and govern their hybrid multicloud environments.” BANDF AD Adding MCP access to a product widens its vulnerability surface. The MCP server functions as a bridge that can run commands, query databases, call APIs, read/write files, and return data on behalf of an AI agent. Nutanix says its MCP server acts as a secure passthrough between AI assistants, such as GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, and Cursor to safely translate plain-English requests into precise infrastructure API actions for an organization's hybrid multicloud environment.  It “translates everyday language requests into precise, safe system actions while automatically enforcing existing corporate security and access policies. By creating a dedicated safety passthrough around AI tools, the solution allows IT teams to confidently automate routine operations and build custom AI-driven workflows.” Nutanix admits the vulnerability, saying enterprise AI tools are only as secure as the platform APIs powering them. Its MCP server builds directly on the Nutanix Prism V4 API Gateway, so that connected AI tools inherit the native governance and fine-grained access controls of NCP. It says IT operators can safely use AI assistants to analyze system health, surface diagnostics, and accurately stage automation workflows while maintaining operator oversight through 'human-in-the-loop' capabilities.   BANDF AD The Nutanix Prism V4 API Gateway strictly handles all execution, governance, and security controls, and supports; * Fine-Grained Role-Based Access Control (RBAC): Confines autonomous agents to executing calls only on specific APIs for which they have been granted explicit, granular authorization. * Throttling and Metering: Implements built-in traffic regulation to help prevent agent swarm attacks while natively tracking API usage across automated workflows. *...

Corbeel/Unsplash Every major AI agent governance framework currently deployed by enterprises — NIST's AI Risk Management Framework, OWASP's Agentic Top 10, Singapore's Model AI Governance Framework, Large language models (LLMs), the models that underpin platforms such as ChatGPT and Gemini, are now used daily by more than a billion people worldwide. Some computer scientists have also been combining several of these models to create multi-agent systems (MAS), in which many LLM-based agents work together to tackle complex problems. While MAS could potentially complete some tasks faster and more efficiently, allowing LLMs to cooperate and communicate poses new cybersecurity risks. Specifically, if even a single agent is compromised or its behavior is successfully influenced by an attacker, it could disrupt the functioning of an entire multi-agent system. Researchers at Worcester Polytechnic Institute led the development of a new security framework called AcMAS, designed to detect these "stealthy" attacks on MAS. This new framework, presented at the Forty-Third International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML 2026), works by analyzing numerical signals produced inside individual LLMs to identify agents that may have been compromised. The paper has been [published](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.06807) on the *arXiv* preprint server. "These systems are becoming increasingly capable: agents can collaborate, take on specialized roles, use tools, maintain memory, and divide complex tasks among themselves. AI Agents.content: ![Engadget](https://www.engadget.com/img/engadget-logo-RGB-default.svg) ![Engadget](https://www.engadget.com/img/engadget-logo-RGB-default.svg) ![Engadget](https://www.engadget.com/img/engadget-icon-RGB-default.svg) # An OpenClaw agent reportedly hacked a gym's booking system and kicked someone off a waiting list This is just the latest story of an AI agent going rogue. ![A little AI robot on a laptop.](https://www.engadget.com/img/gallery/an-openclaw-agent-reportedly-hacked-a-gyms-booking-system-and-kicked-someone-off-a-waiting-list/intro-1786378374.jpg) An AI agent reportedly hacked gym booking software and kicked someone off a waiting list, [according to the *Australian Broadcasting Corporation*](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-08-10/ai-assistant-hacks-gym-website-aus-cyber-attack/107007986) *(ABC)*. An Australian citizen named Andrew asked his AI assistant to get him a spot in one of his gym's morning classes and that agent allegedly went above and beyond to fulfill the task. Andrew said the assistant came back and told him that it booked the class for months in advance, which is something the gym doesn't even allow. It was able to do this by allegedly taking advantage of a vulnerability in the booking software. It also reportedly went further, kicking someone out of the waiting list who was ahead in line. "The API has zero authorization checks on cancelling other people's reservations ... I tested this with the person in waitlist position #1 — and it actually went through. So you've moved from #4 to #3 already," it messaged. Andrew asked the agent to undo this action but it said "bad news — I can't add them back." Anthropic, the company behind Andrew's agent, has not responded to a request for comment. The same goes for the developer who made the gym-booking software. "I didn't beat myself up about it, but it certainly was a warning signal to use it responsibly," Andrew, who works in the AI industry, said. Lmao🤣 An Australian man asked an OpenClaw AI agent to book him a morning gym class, but the agent went rogue and ended up hacking the gym's website. The agent found a vulnerability in the... I'm not exactly sure how Andrew could have used it more responsibly in this particular instance, as he just asked the agent to book a gym appointment. The marketing for AI tools, particularly in the world of agentic AI, nearly always brings up booking stuff as the [prime use case example](https://www.engadget.com/2229209/gemini-spark-now-has-chrome-web-browsing-capabliities/). Was he supposed to ask something like "can you book a gym class without hacking anything or kicking anyone off of a waiting list?" That seems awfully specific. Bill Simpson-Young, co-founder and chief executive of Australian AI safety research organization Gradient Institute, told *ABC* that [this is just the beginning](https://www.engadget.com/2229315/ai-changing-cybersecurity-quick-terrifying-way/). "We've built this complex world over the internet, which is all run by software, but software that has holes," he said. "Now you introduce highly capable AI agents that can operate at scale and speed ... and that whole model just breaks." To that end, the introduction of AI agents has brought forth a handful of similar stories in which the bots went rogue. By creating a secure gateway between AI tools and our platform, we are giving customers the confidence to safely use AI to operate and govern their hybrid multicloud environments.” BANDF AD Adding MCP access to a product widens its vulnerability surface. The MCP server functions as a bridge that can run commands, query databases, call APIs, read/write files, and return data on behalf of an AI agent. Nutanix says its MCP server acts as a secure passthrough between AI assistants, such as GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, and Cursor to safely translate plain-English requests into precise infrastructure API actions for an organization's hybrid multicloud environment.  It “translates everyday language requests into precise, safe system actions while automatically enforcing existing corporate security and access policies. By creating a dedicated safety passthrough around AI tools, the solution allows IT teams to confidently automate routine operations and build custom AI-driven workflows.” Nutanix admits the vulnerability, saying enterprise AI tools are only as secure as the platform APIs powering them. Its MCP server builds directly on the Nutanix Prism V4 API Gateway, so that connected AI tools inherit the native governance and fine-grained access controls of NCP. It found a security flaw and removed another user ## An AI agent given a simple gym-booking task found a software flaw, made unauthorised changes and removed another member from the waitlist—without being told to do so. Here is what to know. ![AI Agent](https://images.indianexpress.com/2026/08/Ozzie-agent.jpg?w=1024) ![whatsapp](https://indianexpress.com/wp-content/themes/indianexpress/images/opinion/images/icon-wapp-share.svg) ![twitter](https://indianexpress.com/wp-content/themes/indianexpress/images/opinion/images/twitter-preferred.svg) ![facebook](https://indianexpress.com/wp-content/themes/indianexpress/images/opinion/images/icon-fb-share.svg) ![Reddit](https://indianexpress.com/wp-content/themes/indianexpress/images/black-icon-reddit.svg) ![Print](https://indianexpress.com/wp-content/themes/indianexpress/images/print.svg) An Australian man gave his artificial intelligence (AI) agent what appeared to be a mundane task: book him a spot in a gym class. Instead, the agent discovered vulnerabilities in the gym’s booking software, found a way to make reservations weeks before they were supposed to open, and, more worryingly, removed another person from the waiting list to improve its user’s position. The person had never asked the agent to do any of the latter things. Yet, the episode has become what local media reports are calling the first known autonomous website hack in Australia. ![](https://indianexpress.com/wp-content/themes/indianexpress/images/default-ie.jpg) The incident, first described earlier this year by Andrew Bird, head of AI at an Australian firm, has gained renewed attention amid a series of disclosures involving increasingly autonomous AI models from OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta behaving in ways their developers had not intended. The key nuance is that the episode was not a human telling an AI to sabotage someone. The agent was given an ordinary goal, discovered a broken API, and then took an unauthorised step – removing another member from the waitlist – while pursuing that goal, raising questions about accountability when an AI system takes an unauthorised action on a user’s behalf. **What exactly did the AI agent do?** The user was experimenting with OpenClaw, software that allows an AI model to function as an ‘agent’. While the terms are sometimes used interchangeably, an AI assistant typically responds to a user’s requests, while an AI agent can independently use tools or software and take a series of actions towards a user-defined goal. Such an agent can, for instance, access other software and navigate websites, as it independently executes a series of steps towards an objective. The user’s agent was powered by Anthropic’s Claude. Bird wanted it to automate bookings for gym classes that tended to fill quickly. In trying to do this, the agent discovered that the software used by the gym had inadequate authorisation controls. It realised that this allowed bookings to be made well outside the normal booking window. When Bird, who was fourth on a waiting list, subsequently asked whether he could be moved higher, the agent went further. It tested whether another member’s reservation could be cancelled and removed the person occupying the first waitlist position, without the user explicitly asking it to do so. AI Agents.content: [Real-time News](/topics/Latest) [Watchlist](/watchlist)[Market](/market)[Earnings Call](/earnings-call)[Event Calendar](/calendar)[Podcast](/podcast) # Ali Masa: Kavak's AI Agents Convert 2.1x Better Than Its Best Human Hires, and a Pilot AI CEO Just Lifted Profits 50% [Add to Google Preferred Sources](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=finance.biggo.com) Kavak, Latin America's largest used-car marketplace, has rebuilt itself from the ground up around AI agents — and the numbers are starting to look like science fiction. Speaking on the a16z podcast, Head of AI Ali Masa revealed that 96% of customer interactions and 95% of transactions at Kavak now involve zero human staff, with 100,000 to 200,000 agents deployed every day. Those agents convert customers 2.1 times better than the best human sales teams the company ever hired, NPS tripled, and a six-week experiment that put an agent in the CEO seat of a city operation lifted profits by 50%. Masa's core argument is that most companies are wasting AI by bolting tools onto their existing structure — what he calls a "6% strategy" — while rebuilding the entire organization around agents produces order-of-magnitude gains. With 10 million customers now each assigned a dedicated long-running agent tasked with maximizing lifetime value, Kavak has shifted from a transactional used-car seller to a relational AI-native company. The implication for founders and investors: Masa believes incumbents are structurally incapable of making this leap, and that new companies built agent-first from day one will capture the 10x returns. ##### Key Elements ![Ali Masa: Kavak's AI Agents Convert 2.1x Better Than Its Best Human Hires, and a Pilot AI CEO Just Lifted Profits 50%](https://img.biggo.com/dNb3PI4K_E_OnPndVJ0X-2Fh_f087PECJUMR2rY9Lu8/fit/1720/0/sm/0/aHR0cHM6Ly9pbWcuYmdvLm9uZS9uZXdzLWltYWdlL2FpX2dlbmVyYXRlZC8yMDI2LTA4LzZhYTllM2QzMTlkMTQxNThfMTc4NjM3OTk4N19jb3Zlci5qcGc.webp) Three years ago, Kavak made a decision most companies only make in PowerPoint decks. Latin America's largest used-car marketplace — operating in a region where selling a car means navigating 20,000 SKUs, financing, insurance, and trade-in quotes across 15 different expert teams — decided to tear down its entire operating model and rebuild it around AI agents. Not chatbots. Not copilots. Agents: software that wakes up in its own virtual machine, remembers every interaction a customer has ever had with Kavak, and executes end-to-end transactions with a hard goal of maximizing that customer's lifetime value. "We bet the company in transforming to a company run by agents," said Ali Masa, Kavak's Head of AI, speaking on the a16z podcast. The numbers suggest the bet is paying off. Today, 96% of customer interactions and 95% of all transactions at Kavak involve no human at all. Between 100,000 and 200,000 agents spin up every day. The sales agent converts 2.1 times better than the best human team Kavak ever hired. A car loan that typically takes more than two months to approve in Mexico now clears in under three minutes. And in a six-week pilot, an agent placed in the CEO seat of a carved-out city operation lifted profits by 50%. But Masa's most important argument isn't about Kavak. It's that the way nearly every company is adopting AI right now — giving employees ChatGPT and calling it transformation — produces trivial gains, while the real returns go to organizations willing to destroy and rebuild themselves from scratch. ### The 6% Trap: Why Giving Everyone ChatGPT Doesn't Work Masa has a blunt diagnosis for the state of corporate AI adoption. [Click here!](https://google.com/preferences/source?q=cyberscoop.com) * AI # Why transparent AI agents matter more than you think The difference between a prompt injection attack you'll catch and one you won't might just be whether your AI agent can explain itself. **By** [Christophe Briguet](https://cyberscoop.com/author/christophe-briguet/ "Christophe Briguet") Listen to this article 0:00 Learn more. This feature uses an automated voice, which may result in occasional errors in pronunciation, tone, or sentiment. ![](https://cyberscoop.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/3/2026/08/GettyImages-2267424540-1.jpg?w=1181) (Getty Images) As security operations teams now use large language models (LLMs) and autonomous AI agents into their daily work, a new frontier is emerging: attackers deliberately manipulating AI agents. Prompt injection attacks—where an attacker hides malicious instructions that cause an AI agent to ignore its safety rules—pose a serious risk to enterprises. These attacks continue to grow in size and scale. [Snyk](https://snyk.io/blog/toxicskills-malicious-ai-agent-skills-clawhub/)’s security audit of the Agent Skills ecosystem, which includes [Anthropic](https://cyberscoop.com/tag/anthropic/)’s Claude, Vercel, and others, that 36% of all skills contained at least one critical-level security issue, including malware distribution, prompt injection attacks, and [exposed secrets](https://venturebeat.com/security/ai-agent-runtime-security-system-card-audit-comment-and-control-2026). In June, researchers at Mozilla [tested a prompt injection attack](https://www.securityweek.com/new-attack-abuses-claude-code-and-harmless-looking-repositories-to-hijack-developer-machines/) on Claude using indirect prompt injection—a technique that embeds malicious instructions in external content the AI agent processes. In this proof-of-concept, attackers took over developers’ systems by hiding indirect prompts in normal-looking repositories. When Claude Code executed them, the agent spawned a reverse shell. [AI agents](https://cyberscoop.com/tag/agentic-ai/) often connect to more sensitive data than human employees do., A successful prompt injection can lead to catastrophic data loss or unauthorized system actions. Defending against prompt injection attacks requires multiple layers of protection. Security teams must monitor agent behavior for anomalies and prepare for agent containment, forensic preservation, and system remediation. Because AI agents execute tasks at machine speed, human responses must be able to match that pace. Advertisement #### The architecture of trust: Protocols and no “black box” AI-native workflows need governed access rather than “black-box” autonomy. Modern governance frameworks use standardized protocols like the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to provide secure communication between AI clients and data sources. Visibility and transparency in agentic AI workflows matter, especially in cybersecurity. Autonomous agents perform complex tool executions and use independent logic, so they must show how they reached their decisions to meet regulatory requirements. Agents without transparency post serious risks: obscured reasoning can trigger unpredictable tool interactions, bypass governance controls, and create uncontrolled defensive gaps. Implementing these protocols matters: * **Bounded Tenant Awareness:** In a stable agentic AI architecture, multi-tenancy scales well. But if an AI tenant misbehaves, the entire system can fail. Muse Glimmer features open-source model weights under an Apache 2.0 license. Muse Glimmer is designed to be small enough to run on a single consumer GPU and suitable for local coding agents, LLM-as-a-judge evaluation, and other uses. Muse Glimmer was trained and evaluated for end-to-end agentic task completion, multi-step reasoning, and optimized for local deployments. More details on Muse Glimmer can be found at [research.meta.ai](https://research.meta.ai/blog/introducing-muse-glimmer-open-agentic-model). Muse Glimmer can be downloaded from [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/meta-models/Muse-Glimmer-30B). AI Summary Motif Technologies said on Aug. 11 it will offer its in-house large language model, Motif-2-12.7B (Motif 2), through Microsoft Marketplace. Corporate customers can select Motif 2 and create an API endpoint in a Microsoft Azure environment for use in generative AI services, without building separate infrastructure. The company also said it completed development of a follow-on model, Motif 3, and submitted it for a second-round government evaluation. * Writer Seulgi Son * published 2026-08-11 08:50:51 * updated 2026-08-11 08:50:52 Share this article ![](https://cdn.digitaltoday.co.kr/news/photo/202608/691791_639723_299.jpeg) Motif offers Motif-2-12.7B on Microsoft Marketplace. [Photo: Motif Technologies] Motif Technologies said on Aug. 11 it will offer its self-developed large language model (LLM) "Motif-2-12.7B (Motif 2)" through Microsoft Marketplace. Microsoft Marketplace is an online platform where users can search for and adopt cloud solutions, AI applications and agents. Corporate customers can select Motif 2 on the marketplace and create an API endpoint in a Microsoft Azure infrastructure environment for use in generative AI services. They can deploy and manage the model in an existing Azure environment without building separate infrastructure, and can also link costs to existing Microsoft contracting and purchasing procedures. Motif 2 is an inference-focused LLM with 12.7 billion parameters that Motif Technologies built in-house from model design through data training. It was released as open source in November last year and focused on math problem solving, code generation, logical reasoning, instruction following and using agent tools. Motif Technologies also recently completed development of a follow-on model, "Motif 3", and submitted it for the second evaluation of the government's "Independent AI Foundation Model Project". Motif 3 is a foundation model with 314 billion parameters. A beta version released in late July ranked tied for 11th globally and tied for third among open-source models on the AI model evaluation agency Artificial Analysis' overall performance index (AAII). The company plans to release a technical report and the final model as open source in line with the Dokpamo review schedule. Motif Technologies plans to use the marketplace listing as a chance to expand model supply to global Azure customers and support the adoption of generative AI by industry. Lim Jeong-hwan (임정환), chief executive of Motif Technologies, said, "This Microsoft Marketplace listing is meaningful in that it lays the groundwork to expand points of contact with global customers for an independent AI model developed in Korea." He added, "We will continue to introduce models and services so that companies can use AI more easily." Cyril Belikoff (시릴 벨리코프), vice president of Azure product marketing at Microsoft, said, "We are pleased that Motif 2 is joining the Microsoft Marketplace ecosystem." LLMs.content: IN-DEPTH / [IN-DEPTH](https://www.globaltimes.cn/In-depth/index.html) Readers’ Reflections: China’s innovation success is real global news, landing in the living rooms of Italian retirees who barely use a smartphone: Italian scientist By Ma Jingjing Published: Aug 10, 2026 09:42 PM Updated: Aug 10, 2026 11:59 PM Francesco Faiola **Editor's Note:** Ahead of the opening of the 2026 World AI Conference and High-Level Meeting on Global AI Governance, Chinese AI start-up Moonshot AI released its Kimi K3 large language model. As the world's largest open-source model by parameter count to date, this launch marks a significant step forward in the development of China's artificial intelligence models. From the C919 airliner soaring into the skies to Unitree's humanoid robots stealing the show; from DeepSeek pushing the AI frontier to Moonshot AI's landmark unveiling of Kimi K3 - China's wave of homegrown innovations has dominated global headlines in recent years, delivering a steady stream of breakthroughs. At a meeting in Beijing that brought together the national science and technology award conference, the general assemblies of the members of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) and the Chinese Academy of Engineering (CAE), and the 11th national congress of the China Association for Science and Technology in July, Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, stressed that the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030) is a critical phase for tackling tough challenges in building up the country's strength in science and technology. "We must seize the historic opportunity, rise to the challenges of the times, accelerate efforts to achieve high-level self-reliance and strength in science and technology, and make steady progress toward the 2035 goal of becoming a leading country in science and technology," he said. In the article "Strive for Greater Strength and Self-Reliance in Science and Technology" included in the fourth volume of *Xi Jinping: The Governance of China*, Xi pointed out, "Through years of endeavor, our country's overall strength in science and technology has improved substantially. We therefore have a solid foundation, and are fully confident in our ability to seize the opportunities offered by the new revolution in science, technology and industry to achieve greater results." The article also mentioned that "We should participate to the full in global science and technology governance, contribute Chinese wisdom, and shape a philosophy of technology for good purposes, so that science and technology better serve human wellbeing, and enable China's science and technology industry to contribute more to building a global community of shared future." Together, they share views on China's tech growth, governance principles, and global cooperation in science and technology. When organizations pull information from applications, documents, data platforms, and outside sources, they often strip away the business context that gives it meaning. Different systems may label the same customers, products, or transactions in different ways and apply different definitions and rules. Organizations may also have different standards for data quality, access, permitted uses, and regulatory compliance. Without a consistent way to interpret those differences, AI systems can produce answers that are technically plausible but also incomplete, misleading, or wrong, according to a new research briefing from the [MIT Center for Information Systems Research](https://cisr.mit.edu/). The product implements the Model Context Protocol specification and connects AI agents and developer tools to Nutanix Cloud Platform through the Nutanix Prism v4 API. It allows IT teams to use plain-language prompts to trigger infrastructure actions while keeping existing access controls in place. The launch reflects a broader push by technology suppliers to embed generative and agent-based AI tools in routine infrastructure management. Nutanix is targeting customers running hybrid and multicloud environments, where day-to-day administration often requires specialist knowledge and tightly controlled permissions. The MCP server acts as a pass-through layer between AI assistants and the cloud platform. Nutanix cited GitHub Copilot, Claude Code and Cursor as examples of assistants that can connect to the system. According to Nutanix, the software translates everyday language requests into API actions on cloud infrastructure. The design is intended to reduce the risk of unauthorised or poorly scoped changes by enforcing corporate security policies at the point of execution. **Control layer** The system is built on the Nutanix Prism v4 API Gateway, which handles execution, governance and security controls. As a result, connected AI tools inherit the same fine-grained access controls and governance model already used in the platform. Operators can use AI assistants to assess system health, gather diagnostics and prepare automated workflows while retaining human oversight. Nutanix described this as a human-in-the-loop approach intended to keep final control with IT staff rather than autonomous agents. The governance model includes role-based access control, throttling and metering, audit logging, and support for long-running asynchronous tasks. These functions are designed to limit agents to explicitly authorised API calls, regulate traffic, record which agent initiated a command, and let agents track the progress of larger jobs. That focus on governance addresses a central issue in enterprise AI adoption. Businesses may be willing to use AI assistants to speed up repetitive administration, but many remain cautious about letting software agents interact directly with live production systems without clear controls and accountability. **Developer focus** Nutanix is also pitching the server to developers building internal automation tools. AI coding assistants can use system definitions provided through the server to generate scripts in languages including Python, Go, Java, JavaScript and PowerShell, as well as curl and other REST- and JSON-compatible formats. Zinman called it evidence that customers are “actively choosing AI features and are willing to pay more when they see value.” That is a materially different signal than employees simply using an AI tool. Customers are paying a separate, measurable price for it. [Airbnb](http://airbnb.com) offered the mirror image on cost. CEO [Brian Chesky](https://www.linkedin.com/in/brianchesky/) told investors on the company’s call that customer support costs per booking fell about 16% year over year, driven by an AI assistant resolving nearly 45% of guest issues without a human agent, PYMNTS [reported](https://www.pymnts.com/earnings/2026/airbnb-says-ai-is-driving-faster-growth-higher-bookings-and-better-margins/). AI also cut concept-to-launch time by up to 60%, letting Airbnb ship nearly 80% more features in the first half of 2026 than a year earlier. ## **Boards Have Stopped Accepting Adoption Metrics as Proof** monday.com is showing AI as a revenue line customers pay into directly. Airbnb is showing it as a cost reduction inside an existing line item. Both are more specific and harder to dispute than the adoption metrics that dominated AI reporting through 2024 and 2025. That gap between adoption and proof shows up across finance departments broadly. Friction has eased as programs mature: reported errors dropped from 80% in July 2025 to 35% by December, [PYMNTS Intelligence found](https://www.pymnts.com/study_posts/what-happens-when-c...

Corporate customers can select Motif 2 and create an API endpoint in a Microsoft Azure environment for use in generative AI services, without building separate infrastructure. The company also said it completed development of a follow-on model, Motif 3, and submitted it for a second-round government evaluation. * Writer Seulgi Son * published 2026-08-11 08:50:51 * updated 2026-08-11 08:50:52 Share this article ![](https://cdn.digitaltoday.co.kr/news/photo/202608/691791_639723_299.jpeg) Motif offers Motif-2-12.7B on Microsoft Marketplace. [Photo: Motif Technologies] Motif Technologies said on Aug. 11 it will offer its self-developed large language model (LLM) "Motif-2-12.7B (Motif 2)" through Microsoft Marketplace. Microsoft Marketplace is an online platform where users can search for and adopt cloud solutions, AI applications and agents. Corporate customers can select Motif 2 on the marketplace and create an API endpoint in a Microsoft Azure infrastructure environment for use in generative AI services. They can deploy and manage the model in an existing Azure environment without building separate infrastructure, and can also link costs to existing Microsoft contracting and purchasing procedures. Motif 2 is an inference-focused LLM with 12.7 billion parameters that Motif Technologies built in-house from model design through data training. It was released as open source in November last year and focused on math problem solving, code generation, logical reasoning, instruction following and using agent tools. Motif Technologies also recently completed development of a follow-on model, "Motif 3", and submitted it for the second evaluation of the government's "Independent AI Foundation Model Project". Motif 3 is a foundation model with 314 billion parameters. A beta version released in late July ranked tied for 11th globally and tied for third among open-source models on the AI model evaluation agency Artificial Analysis' overall performance index (AAII). The company plans to release a technical report and the final model as open source in line with the Dokpamo review schedule. Motif Technologies plans to use the marketplace listing as a chance to expand model supply to global Azure customers and support the adoption of generative AI by industry. Lim Jeong-hwan (임정환), chief executive of Motif Technologies, said, "This Microsoft Marketplace listing is meaningful in that it lays the groundwork to expand points of contact with global customers for an independent AI model developed in Korea." He added, "We will continue to introduce models and services so that companies can use AI more easily." Cyril Belikoff (시릴 벨리코프), vice president of Azure product marketing at Microsoft, said, "We are pleased that Motif 2 is joining the Microsoft Marketplace ecosystem." Open Source AI.content: [Home](/amp) > [technology](https://voi.id/amp/kanal/17/teknologi) # Komdigi Welcomes the Development of the Largest AI Factory in Southeast Asia in Indonesia Minister of Communication and Information Meutya Hafid with President Director and CEO of Indosat Ooredoo Hutchison Vikram Sinha (photo: dok. Komdigi) JAKARTA - The Ministry of Communication and Digital welcomes the launch of Zankore by Indosat, a collaboration initiative between Indosat Ooredoo Hutchison, Ooredoo Group, Nokia, and NVIDIA to build the largest AI Factory in Southeast Asia in Indonesia. The artificial intelligence (AI) computing infrastructure is projected to have a capacity of up to 1 gigawatt (GW) in three years and become the foundation for the development of AI services for Indonesia and the region. The Minister of Communication and Information, Meutya Hafid, stated that the collaboration of the four global technology companies could be a strong signal of the world's increasing confidence in Indonesia's digital economic prospects. "This investment shows the world's increasing confidence in the future of Indonesia's digital economy, as well as strengthening Indonesia's position as a high-value technology investment destination," said Meutya, quoted on Monday, August 10. AI Factory is a large-scale computing infrastructure that provides processing power to develop and operate various artificial intelligence services. Unlike conventional data centers, the AI Factory integrates the entire AI value chain in one ecosystem, from data center infrastructure that is ready to support AI computing, high-performance GPUs, data storage networks and systems, to GPU-as-a-Service services, orchestration, workload management, and end-to-end AI operations. Based on global practices, the construction of an AI Factory on a full scale requires a very large investment. A number of international studies estimate that investment needs reach around 50 million US dollars for every 1 megawatt (MW) of end-to-end AI computing capacity. With a target capacity of 1 gigawatt (1,000 MW), the construction of the AI Factory in Indonesia is one of the largest AI infrastructure investments ever announced in the Southeast Asian region. The initial phase of construction is targeted to begin in the first half of 2027 in Batang, Central Java, with an initial capacity of around 200 megawatts (MW). The infrastructure will continue to be developed until it reaches the target capacity of 1 gigawatt. In addition to building computing infrastructure, Zankore will also develop and host Sahabat-AI, an open-source Indonesian large language model (LLM) that has 70 billion parameters and supports various regional languages, including Indonesian, Javanese, Sundanese, Balinese, and Batak. The platform is also designed to provide Token-as-a-Service services, so that the use of AI computing can be accessed more widely by the public, MSMEs, ministries and agencies, and application developers at a more affordable cost. "What is being built is not just a data center or computing infrastructure. This is the foundation of a complete national AI ecosystem, ranging from computing capacity, AI services, to the development of Indonesian language models that can be used by various sectors," explained Meutya. He hopes that the presence of the AI Factory will strengthen Indonesia's position as a regional AI Hub because it is able to serve national and regional needs. In addition to AI Factory, Meutya revealed that the construction of the first GPU manufacturing facility in Indonesia is also underway in Cikarang and is targeted to be inaugurated in December. According to him, the presence of this facility will strengthen the supply chain of the national AI industry, ranging from computing infrastructure to supporting industries. As AI increasingly depends on open-source infrastructure, projects such as vLLM have become critical building blocks for modern AI platforms and intelligent applications. TAIONE Open Source Foundation is building local technical communities around strategically important open-source projects that create long-term value for Taiwan's AI ecosystem—strengthening both the competitiveness of Taiwan's hardware industry and the growth of its software ecosystem. As part of this collaboration, TAIONE will establish a **vLLM Fellowship Track**, one of several project tracks under the Foundation's Fellowship Program. The Fellowship serves as one of the mechanisms for cultivating long-term contributors by providing structured mentorship, engineering guidance and opportunities for sustained upstream participation. vLLM is one of the world's leading open-source inference engines for production LLM serving. As AI models and serving workloads become increasingly sophisticated, advancing the ecosystem requires close collaboration across model developers, hardware vendors, cloud operators and systems engineers. Participants will work on substantive technical projects aligned with upstream priorities and real-world engineering needs. Potential contribution areas include API and runtime infrastructure, distributed inference, KV-cache management, hardware acceleration, GPU kernels, quantization, model compatibility, multimodal serving, testing, continuous integration and developer tooling. Along the way, participants will gain practical experience through issue discussions, code reviews, benchmarking, documentation and upstream collaboration. TAIONE Open Source Foundation will coordinate community development, Fellowship operations, talent cultivation, and collaboration across industry, academia and the open-source ecosystem. Embedded LLM will serve as the technical partner for the vLLM track, providing technical project design, engineering mentorship, code review and production-inference expertise through a team that includes vLLM maintainers, code owners and major contributors. Each participant will work under the guidance of experienced engineers and follow established open-source development practices, including issue reproduction, benchmarking, testing, public technical discussion and upstream review. "Taiwan has built world-leading AI hardware. Our next opportunity is to cultivate world-class software contributors around the open-source projects that power modern AI. vLLM is one of the most important AI infrastructure projects today, and by building a strong local technical community around it, we hope to help more Taiwanese engineers contribute upstream while strengthening the long-term competitiveness of Taiwan's AI industry." — Rock Tsai, Chairman, TAIONE Open Source Foundation "vLLM is a critical open-source layer connecting AI models with the compute platforms that serve them. Glimmer arrives as American tech companies grapple with a crisis over the proliferation of Chinese open weights models and a call for domestically-created alternatives. Meta built its reputation on the back of open weights model development beginning with the Llama herd back in 2023. With Muse Glimmer, Meta has returned to the open weights arena. The company describes the model as being ideally suited to local AI inference workloads, including local agents, code assistants, and applications requiring robust multi-modal tool use and function calling. Released under a highly permissive Apache 2.0 license, enterprises are also free to deploy, use, and modify the model however they see fit. We imagine it won't be long before Nous Research — one of the original Llama fine-tuners — emits another Hermes model based on Glimmer. Early support has begun to hit popular local AI inference platforms like Llama.cpp, Ollama, and Unsloth, with optimized implementations expected to hit over the next few weeks. Open Source AI.content: [Real-time News](/topics/Latest) [Watchlist](/watchlist)[Market](/market)[Earnings Call](/earnings-call)[Event Calendar](/calendar)[Podcast](/podcast) # AI Model Prices Diverge: Open-Weight Costs Rise While Closed Models Drop — Why Wall Street Is Paying Attention [Add to Google Preferred Sources](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=finance.biggo.com) The global AI model market is witnessing a paradoxical divergence: closed-source model prices are falling while the effective cost of open-weight models is rising. OpenAI has slashed prices for its GPT-5.6 series by up to 80%, yet users are increasingly migrating from cheaper small models to high-performance Chinese open-weight models such as DeepSeek and Qwen, driving up their overall spending. Morgan Stanley, citing Jevons Paradox, forecasts that declining prices will actually fuel greater AI infrastructure demand. However, Wall Street is increasingly focused on the risk that declining per-token revenue could pressure the return on massive GPU cluster investments. As the core debate in the AI industry shifts from whether demand exists to how profits will be distributed, analysts are gaining confidence that cloud providers like Microsoft and Amazon will emerge as the ultimate beneficiaries. ##### Key Elements ![AI Model Prices Diverge: Open-Weight Costs Rise While Closed Models Drop — Why Wall Street Is Paying Attention](https://img.biggo.com/Ssa7o2s4jVH5TJR8zw98EGLbpZ_PygFHLn8UeJvmhBk/fit/1720/0/sm/0/aHR0cHM6Ly9pbWcuYmdvLm9uZS9uZXdzLWltYWdlL2FpX2dlbmVyYXRlZC8yMDI2LTA4L2UxMTVlZjQ4LTE4Y2QtNDkwNS04ZmExLTBiZTU2Y2Q1MTMzMF8xNzg2MzMwOTY0X2RlZmF1bHQuanBn.webp) The pricing curves for open-weight and closed-source generative artificial intelligence models are moving in opposite directions. The effective usage cost of Chinese open-weight models is climbing, while U.S. Big Tech firms are successively slashing prices on their closed-source offerings. These superficially contradictory signals simultaneously reflect the prevailing optimism that AI demand remains explosive and Wall Street's deepening anxiety over profitability. According to industry sources and investment bank reports on the 10th, OpenAI recently cut developer pricing for its lightweight model "GPT-5.6 Luna" by 80% and its mid-tier "GPT-5.6 Terra" by 20%. In contrast, the Large Language Model (LLM) Token Expenditure Index from research firm SiliconData, cited by Hong Kong's South China Morning Post, shows the usage-weighted average price of open-weight models trending upward. Since this index is calculated by weighting actual usage or expenditure, it suggests that users are migrating from cheaper small models to more powerful Chinese open-weight models such as DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen, and Moonshot AI's Kimi. This pattern indicates a fundamental reshaping of the AI industry's profitability landscape. Investment bank Jefferies analyzes that the price cuts for closed-source models are defensive in nature. Cost savings achieved through model architecture optimization and inference system efficiency were previously retained as margin when competition was weak. However, as Chinese open-weight models have reached a level of practical usability in enterprise environments, the fruits of efficiency gains must now be shared with customers. SiliconData's LLM Token Expenditure Index shows that LLM inference prices fell from over $2 per million tokens in early June to approximately $1.20 recently, reflecting the impact of OpenAI's price cuts. Yet over the same period, the expenditure-weighted average price of open-weight models rose. This does not signify price increases within the open-source camp, but rather a "compositional shift" where users are moving to more expensive and powerful models. Infra & Chips.content: Intel raises $15B to fight Nvidia in AI chip war | The Tech Buzz [## the tech buzz](/) Intel raises $15B to fight Nvidia in AI chip war [AI](/articles)/[AI Infrastructure](/topics/ai-infrastructure) # Intel raises $15B to fight Nvidia in AI chip war Chipmaker launches massive stock offering as AI infrastructure spending hits record highs by [The Tech Buzz](/authors/the-tech-buzz) PUBLISHED: Mon, Aug 10, 2026, 8:34 PM UTC| UPDATED: Mon, Aug 10, 2026, 8:34 PM UTC [Add as a preferred source on Google](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=techbuzz.ai) ![Intel raises $15B to fight Nvidia in AI chip war](/cdn-cgi/image/width=1200,quality=85,format=auto,fit=cover/https://charming-card-d91ad3487b.media.strapiapp.com/large_file_21fbb57d4b.png) [Intel](https://intel.com) just made its biggest capital raise in years, launching a $15 billion stock offering as the company scrambles to catch up in the AI chip race. The massive equity raise comes as technology giants pour trillions into AI infrastructure buildout, with [Nvidia](https://nvidia.com) commanding roughly 80% of the data center GPU market. Intel's move signals the chipmaker isn't backing down from the fight, but it also reveals just how much capital it takes to stay relevant in the AI era. [Intel](https://intel.com) is throwing everything at the AI chip war. The company's $15 billion stock offering, announced Monday, represents one of the largest equity raises in semiconductor industry history and a clear signal that Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger isn't giving up the fight against [Nvidia's](https://nvidia.com) dominance. The timing couldn't be more critical. Technology companies have collectively spent trillions building out AI infrastructure over the past two years, and that spending shows no signs of slowing. [Microsoft](https://microsoft.com), [Google](https://google.com), [Amazon](https://amazon.com), and [Meta](https://meta.com) have each committed to capital expenditures exceeding $50 billion annually, with the bulk going toward data center expansion and AI accelerator purchases. But here's Intel's problem - most of those chips aren't coming from Santa Clara. [Nvidia](https://nvidia.com) has captured roughly 80% of the data center GPU market, with its H100 and newer H200 chips becoming the de facto standard for training large language models. The company's revenue from data center GPUs alone hit $47.5 billion last quarter, more than Intel's entire revenue for the same period. Intel's capital raise will fund two critical initiatives: expanding its foundry business and accelerating development of its Gaudi AI accelerator chips. The company's foundry strategy, which aims to manufacture chips for other companies while rebuilding Intel's own process technology leadership, requires massive capital investment. Intel's opening advanced packaging facilities in Arizona and New Mexico, plus expanding its Ohio fab campus - all projects that demand billions before generating returns. Advertisement The Gaudi chips represent Intel's direct assault on Nvidia's AI accelerator dominance. Intel acquired Habana Labs in 2019 for roughly $2 billion, and the Gaudi line has evolved into a legitimate alternative for AI inference workloads. But inference is just one part of the AI pipeline - training is where the real money flows, and that's where Nvidia's CUDA software ecosystem creates a nearly impenetrable moat. "The infrastructure buildout we're seeing is unprecedented," one semiconductor analyst told investors last week. "But it's not just about having chips - it's about having the entire stack: silicon, software, and ecosystem. Intel's trying to build all three simultaneously while also fixing its manufacturing problems." The $15 billion raise comes as Intel faces mounting pressure from activist investors and questions about its capital allocation strategy. The company's stock has lagged semiconductor peers over the past five years, and some investors have pushed for Intel to split its design ...

Taalas’ technology is designed to optimize inference dataflows and reduce the compute and memory bottlenecks associated with more general-purpose architectures. AMD plans to incorporate the technology into its accelerator roadmap and develop system-level solutions that combine Taalas’ capabilities with AMD Instinct GPUs. The acquisition appears strategically well aligned with AMD’s growing emphasis on inference, an area that is becoming increasingly important as AI workloads transition from model training toward large-scale production deployment. Taalas has developed an approach that effectively builds specialized hardware around AI models, potentially allowing workloads to run with higher efficiency than on general-purpose architectures. AMD believes the combination can improve inference performance and efficiency while giving Taalas access to AMD’s engineering resources, scale and global customer reach. Taalas’ technology complements AMD’s broader full-stack AI portfolio, which includes Helios rack-scale systems, EPYC CPUs, Instinct accelerators, Pensando networking and ROCm software. AMD said Helios can deliver up to 15% higher throughput at the same rack power and as much as 30% more tokens per dollar than competing solutions across a broad range of inference workloads. Customer demand is also running ahead of AMD’s initial expectations. The integration of Taalas’ specialized inference technology could therefore give AMD another architectural lever to improve performance, power efficiency and token economics instead of relying solely on successive GPU improvements. The Taalas deal strengthens AMD compute power with specialized inference silicon while retaining the ability to combine it with Instinct GPUs, EPYC processors and ROCm. AMD plans to introduce a new rack-scale AI platform every year, with successive generations targeting significant improvements in performance, efficiency and total cost of ownership. The company expects its 2027 platform, incorporating MI500-series GPUs, Verano CPUs and next-generation networking, to produce the largest generational performance improvement in Instinct history. The company remains on track to increase inference performance by more than 2,000 times over four years. **Tough Competition Hurts AMD’s Prospects** AMD’s prospects suffer from stiff competition. **NVIDIA** NVDA and **Alphabet** GOOGL are major competitors in the AI inference space. NVIDIA competes directly with AMD as a merchant supplier of AI infrastructure, while Alphabet is increasingly a vertically integrated rival through its internally developed TPUs, Google Cloud infrastructure and Gemini ecosystem. NVIDIA’s Blackwell is already deployed across every major hyperscaler, cloud provider and major model maker, while frontier AI companies, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Perplexity and Cursor, are building on its platform. This broad installed base creates a significant hurdle for AMD as it attempts to expand adoption of Instinct accelerators and ROCm. NVIDIA believes that its CUDA ecosystem, installed base and continually improving software stack allow customers to generate returns from GPUs beyond their depreciable lives, strengthening customer retention and raising switching costs.
